title: Four-seat 180 mph car
pipeline: carAcceptanceAsync (CAD body, tub, aero build-up, drawings)
brief: Design a car that weighs 2,500 lb, can go 180 mph, seats 4 people, and has a futuristic aerodynamic look.

topSpeed.basis: speed limiter set point (design choice, 295 km/h); without it, the lower of the drag-limited and gear-limited top speeds

disclaimers: Software screening only. Passing software checks is not physical validation; every result below still needs the physical tests listed.
Aerodynamics is a component drag build-up and 2D panel screening, not CFD or wind-tunnel data.

Torsional stiffness is a range: the main solve uses rigid joints (an upper bound). Bond-line springs are computed from the sourced adhesive moduli, and joint-wall distortion is bounded at the EN 1993-1-8 rigid-joint limit (an estimate for this bonded aluminium tub, not a measured stiffness).
caveats: The kerb mass is a lower bound: 40 item(s) the parts' published masses exclude are not in it (see massBreakdown.excluded).

The top speed is a model output (model_output_unvalidated), not a measurement: Cd 0.14542277462919667 is computed (screening range): aero.drag-buildup centre of 0.099..0.214 (not CFD or wind tunnel), frontal area computed from BODY_SHELL (cad.body: projected area of the kernel solid onto the y-z plane), driveline efficiency 0.9 given.

The vehicle top speed (295.0 km/h, 183.3 mph) is the set point of an electronic speed limiter that is a design choice, not built or calibrated; the tyre check relies on its overshoot staying within the 5 km/h design allowance. Without it the model gives 361.1 km/h (224.4 mph, model_output_unvalidated).

The gear limit rests on an estimated redline (7500 rpm): estimated: Ford does not publish a redline for the Gen 4 / Gen 4X crate engines (product pages; the 2020 Mustang technical specification lists the GT's redline as N/A). 7,500 rpm is the Mustang GT tachometer redline since the 2018 (Gen 3) engine as reported from the gauge cluster; the low end is the 7,000 rpm redline of the 2015-2017 (Gen 2) engine reported in the same article.
REQ_mass passes on a lower-bound mass.
REQ_topSpeed passes on a model output (model_output_unvalidated), not a validated top speed: the limited speed (the 295 km/h set point) is reachable only if the unlimited model output holds.

Packaging is screening level: not checked for want of dimensions or design: bellhousing, SUSPENSION_FRONT, SUSPENSION_REAR, STEERING_RACK, EXHAUST, CONTROL_PACK, SEAT_3, SEAT_4, BRAKES_FRONT, BRAKES_REAR, structural tub, pedal box, dash, steering column, driveshaft, doors, suspension travel.

Assembly packaging fit (meshes are rebuilt from the package spec when the design is opened; the snapshot stores the spec, not the triangles): Packaging fit: warn. head-M95 pass; head-F5 pass; head-M95-rear pass; heel-floor pass; rear-leg pass; four-seats pass; powertrain-cabin pass; powertrain-layout pass; wheel-footwell pass; ingress pass; containment pass; b-pillar pass; cooling-power warn; spare warn; design-quality info. The body is a styling skeleton of monotone cubics (low hood, 60 degree windshield, fastback roof) lofted into the watertight grid. Design check: info, hood at the front axle 0.697 m, silhouette turn 19.9 deg. Layout is ev_skateboard. Range was not specified; 400 km at 160 Wh/km would need 64 kWh, and the floor pack that fits under the heel is about 26.6 kWh at an assumed 250 Wh/L. The library mass tree is still the gasoline car. front_engine stays available and raises the hood where the library radiator and engine clear the skeleton. The viewer loft is not an OpenCascade solid.

checks.method: opening area = sourced radiator core face; air temperature rise from Q = rho * V_fan * cp * dT with dry air at 300 K (Incropera Table A.4) and the coolant-loop heat load. Not a heat-exchanger rating.
warnings: The opening area is the sourced core face. It is not a grille sized to a pressure drop: no grille loss coefficient is published.

The conduction solver is not used. It needs a wall thickness, a conductivity and a convection coefficient. The radiator listing publishes none of those, and its heat rejection is unpublished, so a fin model would be an invented wall.
The air temperature rise is the rise that would carry the estimated coolant heat if the core transferred all of it at the published fan flow. It is not a measured or predicted exit temperature.
Dry-air properties are Table A.4 at 300 K. The coolant screen's design temperature is 90 °C on the liquid side. The two states are not the same fluid.
